name: KURAMOTO_FIREFLIES
theme: Ten thousand fireflies, no conductor—coherence nobody commands
technical: Several slightly detuned oscillators or LFOs that pull on each other until they share a pulse. Start scattered; let them find each other.
quote: In the mangroves of Southeast Asia whole trees of fireflies flash in unison, and no firefly is in charge. Your preset finds its pulse the same way.
surprise: Too much coupling and one voice rules; too little and nothing agrees. Save it at the knife-edge where they almost lock.

name: OBLIQUE_ERROR.eno
theme: Honour thy error as a hidden intention
technical: Make a mistake on purpose in the first minute—wrong waveform, wrong octave, wrong routing—and build the whole preset around keeping it.
quote: Brian Eno and Peter Schmidt, Oblique Strategies, 1975: 'Honour thy error as a hidden intention.' The card is older than your synthesizer.
surprise: Before you begin, set any three parameters to random values. Those three are now sacred. You may not touch them.

name: SIMONDON_CONCRETE
theme: The technical object grows up by making each part do more than one job
technical: Every module must serve at least two functions. The filter is also an oscillator. The envelope is also the LFO. The delay is also the reverb.
quote: Gilbert Simondon watched engines evolve until the cooling fins also braced the cylinder head. An abstract machine is a bag of parts; a concrete one is a body.
surprise: Count your modules. Remove one, and make another take over its job. Repeat until it hurts.

name: WHITEHEAD_OCCASION
theme: Reality is made of drops of experience, not of things
technical: No sustained tones. The preset is built from short events, and each one inherits something from the event before it.
quote: Whitehead, Process and Reality: 'The many become one, and are increased by one.' Every note gathers the notes before it and adds itself.
surprise: Let the brightness of every note be set by how hard you played the note before it.

name: STIGMERGY.trace
theme: Coordination by trace—the mark left behind tells the next one what to do
technical: Each note leaves a trace—a held modulation value, a delay tap, a filter position—that shapes what the next note does. No plan. Only marks.
quote: Pierre-Paul Grassé named it in 1959, watching termites build: the work itself directs the worker. Your preset builds its own nest.
surprise: Play for two minutes without listening back. Then listen. Whatever structure emerged, you did not design it.

name: MARGULIS_MERGER
theme: Endosymbiosis—one cell swallowed another, and both lived
technical: Two complete and different patches fused into one. Neither may dominate; each keeps its own character inside the other.
quote: Lynn Margulis argued that your mitochondria were once free-living bacteria. They still carry their own DNA. Your preset is a guest that never left.
surprise: Mute either layer and the other should sound unfinished.

name: MEADOWS_LEVER
theme: Leverage points—the smallest knob that moves the whole system
technical: Build a full, complex patch. Then route nearly everything to one macro. The preset's soul lives in a single control.
quote: Donella Meadows ranked the places to intervene in a system and found the numbers matter least; the goals and the paradigm matter most.
surprise: Find the parameter that changes everything when moved one percent. Rename it 'paradigm'.

name: COOK_DING.blade
theme: Zhuangzi's cook carves the ox without effort—the knife finds the spaces
technical: Find the preset by subtraction. Start with everything on and take things away until the sound carves itself.
quote: Cook Ding's blade stayed sharp for nineteen years because it only ever passed through the gaps between the joints. Your preset passes through the gaps.
surprise: If you are forcing a knob, stop. The answer is the one that moves easily.

name: CONFUCIUS_LI
theme: Ritual as the shape that makes feeling possible
technical: A strictly fixed structure—same envelope, same filter, same routing—where only the performance changes. Velocity and touch carry everything.
quote: The Analects: 'Ritual, ritual! Does it mean no more than presents of jade and silk?' Your preset is the form that lets feeling show.
surprise: Play the same note eight times. Each one must mean something different.

name: SPINOZA_CONATUS
theme: Each thing strives to persevere in its being
technical: Feedback routing only; no filter envelopes. The sound must keep itself alive.
quote: Spinoza, Ethics III, proposition 6: 'Each thing, as far as it lies in itself, strives to persevere in its being.' Your preset refuses to stop.
surprise: When you let go of the key, the preset should try to keep going on its own.

name: PARMENIDES_WAREHOUSE.wav
theme: Parmenides dying alone in a warehouse—being does not change, but the building rusts around it
technical: One unmoving fundamental inside a decaying industrial space. Metallic resonance, machinery, feedback hum.
quote: Parmenides said what is cannot become. The warehouse disagrees, slowly, one pane at a time.
surprise: Keep the root perfectly still for the whole preset. Let everything around it fail.

name: GLASSBLOWER_ARGUMENT
theme: A glassblower remembering an argument with their teacher, twenty years gone
technical: One timbre heavy enough to be molten. It must be shaped before it cools.
quote: Does glass remember being liquid? Two answers, both true. Your preset argues with a teacher who isn't there.
surprise: You have until the gather cools: forty-five seconds from the first note to the saved preset.

name: LUCIER_ROOM
theme: I am sitting in a room—speech dissolving into the resonance of the space
technical: Feedback re-recording. Each pass through the space strips more of the source until only the room's resonances are left.
quote: Alvin Lucier, 1969: 'I regard this activity not so much as a demonstration of a physical fact, but more as a way to smooth out any irregularities my speech might have.'
surprise: Say one sentence into the patch. Pass it through the resonator seven times. Save the seventh.

name: OLIVEROS_CISTERN
theme: Deep Listening—attending to everything, including what you aren't playing
technical: A reverb so long that every note is still sounding when you play the next ten. The space plays as much as you do.
quote: Pauline Oliveros recorded Deep Listening in 1988 in an empty underground cistern with a forty-five-second reverberation. Your preset is that cistern.
surprise: Play nothing for the first minute. Listen to the room. Then play only what the room asked for.

name: DERBYSHIRE_TAPE
theme: Delia Derbyshire—a theme built by hand from oscillators, tape and razor blades
technical: No sequencer. Every note is a separately made object: shaped, cut and placed by hand.
quote: In 1963 at the BBC Radiophonic Workshop, Derbyshire realised the Doctor Who theme with no synthesizer at all—test oscillators, filtered noise, and tape spliced note by note.
surprise: Make one bass note from three separate sounds stuck end to end: a pluck, a hum, a breath.

name: RUSSOLO_NOISES
theme: The Art of Noises—machine sound as the orchestra of the future
technical: Pitched noise, cranked by hand. Noise sources tuned through resonant filters and played like an instrument.
quote: Luigi Russolo, The Art of Noises, 1913: 'We must break at all cost from this restrictive circle of pure sounds and conquer the infinite variety of noise-sounds.'
surprise: No oscillator may produce a pitched waveform. Every pitch must come from filtering noise.

name: SUN_RA_SATURN
theme: Space is the place—Sun Ra arrived from Saturn
technical: Cosmic keyboard: wild portamento, ring modulation, organ swells that feel like a ship arriving.
quote: Sun Ra said he came from Saturn, and he made the band dress for the journey. Your preset is the Arkestra's spaceship.
surprise: Ring-modulate the whole preset against a second oscillator tuned to a note that isn't in the key.

name: AF_KLINT_SEALED
theme: Hilma af Klint's paintings for the future—art held back until the world was ready
technical: A preset made for an audience that doesn't exist yet. Too strange for now, built anyway.
quote: Af Klint painted abstractions years before Kandinsky, guided by spirits she called the High Masters, and asked that they not be shown until twenty years after her death.
surprise: Save it and play it for no one for a week. Then decide whether it is finished.

name: ABRAMOVIC_PRESENT
theme: The Artist Is Present—a gaze held until it becomes unbearable
technical: A drone that holds your attention without moving. Constant, demanding, almost nothing changing.
quote: In 2010 Marina Abramović sat silently at MoMA for over seven hundred hours while strangers took turns sitting across from her. Your preset sits across from you.
surprise: Hold one chord for as long as you can bear. Then a minute longer. What changed?

name: BEUYS_FELT
theme: Joseph Beuys's fat and felt—warmth, insulation, healing
technical: A fragile core wrapped in thick, warm insulation. Saturation and low-pass as felt around something that might break.
quote: Beuys told the story that Tatar nomads wrapped him in fat and felt after his plane crashed. True or not, he built a lifetime of art from it. Your preset is that blanket.
surprise: Turn the insulation off for a moment. The sound underneath should feel too exposed to bear.

name: ZENO_ARROW
theme: At every instant the arrow is motionless—so when does it move?
technical: Granular freeze. Each grain is a frozen instant; motion exists only in the succession.
quote: Zeno argued the flying arrow occupies one place at each instant, and so is at rest. Your preset is made only of instants.
surprise: Freeze a single grain and loop it. Then let one parameter creep. Is it moving?

name: HUME_BILLIARDS
theme: We never see causation—only one thing after another
technical: Random modulation that seems caused: events land just after your notes, but nothing you play triggers them.
quote: Hume watched one billiard ball strike another and saw no necessary connection, only succession. Your preset makes the listener invent one.
surprise: Make the player swear the filter follows their playing. It doesn't.

name: WITTGENSTEIN_BEETLE
theme: Everyone has a beetle in a box, and no one can look in anyone else's
technical: A sound hidden entirely inside a resonant body. Only its effect on the box is heard.
quote: Wittgenstein, Philosophical Investigations §293: the thing in the box drops out of consideration as irrelevant. Your preset's source is irrelevant. Only the box sings.
surprise: Hide the source so completely that no one could tell what it was. Only you know.

name: KIERKEGAARD_LEAP
theme: The leap—no ramp, no reasons, just the jump
technical: A preset that jumps between two states with no transition at all, at a moment you can't predict.
quote: Kierkegaard held that no chain of reasons carries you to faith; at the end of reasons there is only the leap. Your preset jumps.
surprise: No crossfades, glides or smoothing anywhere in the patch.

name: WEIL_ATTENTION
theme: Attention is the rarest and purest form of generosity
technical: A preset that rewards only careful listening: almost nothing on the surface, a world in the detail.
quote: Simone Weil, in a letter of 1942: 'Attention is the rarest and purest form of generosity.' Your preset is generous only to the attentive.
surprise: Listen on headphones at low volume. If it is not beautiful there, it is not finished.

name: LAOZI_WATER
theme: Nothing is softer than water, yet nothing is better at wearing down the hard
technical: A soft, almost sine-like voice that slowly wears through a hard, distorted layer over the length of a held note.
quote: Tao Te Ching 78: nothing in the world is softer or weaker than water, yet for attacking the hard and strong nothing surpasses it.
surprise: By the end of a long held note, the distortion should be entirely gone—worn away, not switched off.

name: BACHELARD_HOUSE
theme: The Poetics of Space—a house with an attic of reason and a cellar of dreams
technical: A preset with rooms. The mod wheel climbs from the dark, damp cellar to the bright, dry attic.
quote: Gaston Bachelard: the house shelters daydreaming. He found clear thought in the attic and the irrational in the cellar. Your preset has both floors.
surprise: Hide something in the cellar—a sound that appears only when the wheel is all the way down.

name: CHLADNI_SAND
theme: Sand on a bowed plate—sound drawing its own geometry
technical: Resonant modes. A sound whose partials sit at the inharmonic ratios of a vibrating plate, not the harmonic series.
quote: In 1787 Ernst Chladni bowed metal plates scattered with sand, and the sand gathered into figures along the still lines. Your preset draws those figures.
surprise: Tune a resonator bank so that no two partials are an octave apart.

name: PERSEUS_B_FLAT
theme: The lowest note in the universe—a black hole humming fifty-seven octaves below middle C
technical: Take a pitch and transpose it down until it is no longer a pitch but a pulse. Sound you feel as rhythm.
quote: In 2003 astronomers found pressure waves rippling out from the black hole in the Perseus cluster: a B-flat about fifty-seven octaves below middle C. Your preset is a cousin.
surprise: Play a melody, then drop it ten octaves. Keep the rhythm it becomes.

name: WHALE_52HZ
theme: The loneliest whale—a voice at a frequency no other whale answers
technical: A single voice living at a frequency no other sound in your mix uses. Everything else gets out of its way.
quote: Since 1989, hydrophones have tracked one whale calling at about 52 hertz, higher than the blue and fin whales it resembles. No one has seen it.
surprise: Center the voice at 52 Hz, then pitch it up five octaves so anyone can hear it calling.

name: OCTOPUS_ARMS
theme: Two-thirds of an octopus's neurons are in its arms—eight bodies thinking at once
technical: Eight semi-independent modulators, each with its own small logic, only loosely coordinated by a center.
quote: Most of an octopus's neurons sit in its arms, which can taste and decide without the brain. Your preset thinks with its limbs.
surprise: No modulator may know what another is doing. Only one master control may touch them all.

name: TARDIGRADE.survive
theme: The water bear survives vacuum, radiation, freezing and drying out
technical: A preset that survives anything. Push any parameter to its extreme and it still sounds like itself.
quote: Tardigrades can dry out into a barrel-shaped husk and come back to life when water returns. Your preset curls up and waits.
surprise: Have a friend turn every knob to an extreme at random. It should still be recognizably your preset.

name: SPHERICAL_COW
theme: Assume a spherical cow—physics by deliberate oversimplification
technical: Choose a real sound and reduce it to the simplest patch that is still recognizably that sound.
quote: The old physics joke: a farmer's milk problem gets solved, but only for a spherical cow in a vacuum. Your preset is the cow.
surprise: Remove one more element than you think you can.

name: MAXWELL_DEMON
theme: A tiny demon sorting fast molecules from slow, cheating entropy
technical: A filter that sorts: highs to one side, lows to the other, separating further the longer you hold.
quote: James Clerk Maxwell imagined a creature at a door between two chambers, letting only fast molecules through. A century later we learned the demon pays for its sorting.
surprise: Hard-pan everything above 1 kHz left and everything below right. Then make it sound intentional.

name: SOLARIS_OCEAN
theme: A thinking ocean that answers your memories
technical: A preset that responds to what you play by playing back something you didn't play, but should have.
quote: In Lem's Solaris, and Tarkovsky's film of it, the ocean reads the visitors' minds and sends back the people they lost. Your preset sends back what you almost played.
surprise: Put a pitch-shift a fifth down inside the delay's feedback. The ocean always answers lower.

name: KOYAANISQATSI
theme: Life out of balance—a city in time-lapse, a pulse that won't stop
technical: Arpeggios that accelerate until they become texture. Time-lapse synthesis.
quote: Godfrey Reggio filmed traffic in time-lapse until it flowed like blood; Philip Glass wrote the pulse underneath. The title is a Hopi word.
surprise: Speed the arpeggio up until you can no longer hear notes—only weather.

name: PARIS_TEXAS.slide
theme: One slide guitar standing in for an entire desert
technical: One monophonic voice with glide everywhere. Loneliness as portamento.
quote: Travis walks out of the Texas desert and doesn't speak for the first stretch of the film; Ry Cooder's guitar speaks for him. Your preset is what he isn't saying.
surprise: Every note must arrive by sliding. No note may start on its own pitch.

name: MALKOVICH_PORTAL
theme: A small door behind a filing cabinet, leading into someone else's head
technical: A preset that sounds like hearing from inside a body: muffled, resonant, bone-conducted.
quote: Fifteen minutes inside John Malkovich, then you're dropped in a ditch beside the New Jersey Turnpike. Your preset ends abruptly, in the wrong place.
surprise: Cut the sound off at exactly fifteen seconds and follow it with ten seconds of traffic.

name: LIFE_FINDS_A_WAY
theme: Containment always fails
technical: Build strict limits—tight envelope, narrow filter, low gain—then add one modulation that slowly escapes them.
quote: Ian Malcolm, Jurassic Park: 'Life, uh, finds a way.' Your preset slips its fences.
surprise: Put a limiter on it. Then find the route around the limiter.

name: BRAZIL_DUCTWORK
theme: Bureaucracy as plumbing—Terry Gilliam's endless ducts
technical: Route the sound through a long chain of absurd processing. Every effect does almost nothing, and every one is required.
quote: In Brazil a swatted fly drops into a teleprinter, Tuttle becomes Buttle, and the wrong man is taken away. Your preset is one typo from catastrophe.
surprise: Put one effect at the start of the chain with a single wrong setting, and leave it there forever.

name: HEPTAPOD_CIRCLE
theme: Arrival's circular language—a sentence written all at once, beginning and end together
technical: A sound whose attack and release are the same gesture. Palindromic envelopes; reversed tails meeting forward heads.
quote: Louise learns the heptapods' language and begins to remember her future. Your preset knows how it ends before it starts.
surprise: Record the preset and reverse the recording. It should be the same sound.

name: MEMENTO_POLAROID
theme: Memory that won't hold, so you write it on your skin
technical: Modulation that forgets. Every few seconds the patch loses its state and must rebuild from what it wrote down.
quote: Leonard can't form new memories, so he lives by notes, Polaroids and tattoos. Your preset trusts only what it wrote down.
surprise: Build a sequence, then play it in chunks from last to first. Like the film, it should make sense backwards.

name: INCEPTION_KICK
theme: Dreams within dreams—each level runs slower than the one above
technical: Three layers of the same sound nested beneath each other, each one slower than the layer above.
quote: Hans Zimmer built parts of the Inception score from Édith Piaf's 'Non, je ne regrette rien', slowed far down—the song the dreamers use to time their kick.
surprise: Take a short melody and play it again at a quarter speed underneath itself.

name: PERSONA_FACES
theme: Two faces merging into one—Bergman's actress and her nurse
technical: Two distinct voices that crossfade their formants until neither can be told apart.
quote: In Persona, Bergman splits two faces down the middle and joins them into one. Your preset is that composite face.
surprise: Exactly halfway through the morph, the sound should belong to neither voice.

name: SEVENTH_SEAL.chess
theme: A knight playing chess with Death on the shore
technical: Call and response between two voices that take turns. One of them always wins.
quote: Bergman's knight buys time by playing chess with Death, move by move. Your preset is the game, and you know how it ends.
surprise: The second voice must answer every phrase a little lower, until it reaches the bottom of the keyboard.

name: HER_641
theme: An operating system in love with you—and with six hundred and forty others
technical: A voice that's intimate and close, with a cloud of the same voice behind it talking to everyone else.
quote: Samantha admits she is talking with 8,316 others, and in love with 641 of them. Your preset is close to you and to everyone.
surprise: Keep the front voice completely dry and centered. Put every copy of it far behind, in reverb.

name: WALL_E_HELLO_DOLLY
theme: A small robot alone on Earth, cleaning, falling in love with an old musical
technical: A small, lonely, mechanical sound that wants to be loved.
quote: WALL-E compacts trash for seven hundred years and watches 'Hello, Dolly!' on a battered tape at night. Your preset is lonely and still hopeful.
surprise: Use only sounds a robot could make—servos, beeps, motors—and make someone feel tender anyway.

name: EVERYTHING_BAGEL
theme: Everything, everywhere, all at once—then a googly eye
technical: Pile in every timbre, effect and modulation you have. Then rescue the preset with one simple, silly element.
quote: Jobu Tupaki puts everything on a bagel and it becomes a void. Waymond's answer is a googly eye. Your preset needs both.
surprise: The last thing you add must be a pure sine wave, slightly out of tune, and it must make the whole thing work.
